package_info.package_versions: unknown, affected via compromised update channel
package_info.why_malicious: The update mechanism of the NoxPlayer Android emulator was compromised as part of Operation NightScout, enabling attackers to deliver malicious payloads through legitimate software updates. This supply-chain attack targeted millions of users, primarily in online-gaming communities across Asia, and resulted in the installation of malware that enabled espionage, unauthorized remote access, and persistent compromise of affected systems.

execution_context.trigger: During update-time (when the NoxPlayer application checks for and applies updates)
execution_context.file_location: NoxPlayer update package (delivered via the official update channel, but compromised at the source)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The malicious update package, when executed by the NoxPlayer updater, downloads additional malware binaries from attacker-controlled servers, writes them to disk, and executes them without user consent. The payload establishes persistence and enables remote access for espionage.
malicious_snippets.code_language: Windows executable (likely PE format) and/or script (exact language not specified in report)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During update-time, the compromised updater downloads additional binaries from attacker-controlled servers, writes them to disk, and executes them, resulting in persistent remote access and enabling espionage on the victim system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The update process downloads and executes binaries from domains not associated with the official NoxPlayer infrastructure, bypassing signature verification and user consent. This is a hallmark of supply-chain attacks and is highly anomalous for legitimate software updates.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate update mechanisms only download and execute updates that are cryptographically signed and verified by the vendor, and do not fetch or run arbitrary binaries from external, untrusted sources. In this case, the updater was abused to deliver and execute unsigned, unexpected payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download and install updates, but only from trusted, verified sources and with proper signature validation. Downloading and executing arbitrary code from unknown servers is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Update process initiates network connections to non-official or previously unknown domains/IPs during update
Unsigned or unexpected binaries are written to disk and executed by the updater
No user notification or consent for the execution of additional payloads
Update package contents differ from official manifests or lack proper digital signatures

attack_chain.action: Attackers compromise the NoxPlayer update infrastructure, allowing them to inject malicious update packages into the official update channel.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious update packages are delivered to user systems via the legitimate update process.

attack_chain.action: The compromised NoxPlayer updater downloads and executes additional malware from attacker-controlled servers during the update process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware is installed on victim systems, establishing persistence, enabling espionage, and potentially allowing further lateral movement or data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Update process initiates outbound network connections to domains or IPs not associated with official NoxPlayer infrastructure during update
Execution of unsigned or unexpected binaries by the update process immediately after an update
Creation of new processes or persistence mechanisms by the updater that are not part of the official update
file_indicators: Unexpected binaries written to disk by the update process (file names and paths not present in official update manifests)
Modified or unsigned update packages delivered via the update channel
Presence of files or executables in NoxPlayer directories that are not part of legitimate updates
network_indicators: Outbound connections from the update process to domains or IP addresses not registered to NoxPlayer or its parent company
Network traffic to known C2 or suspicious remote servers during or immediately after the update process
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the NoxPlayer update process for network activity to non-official domains or IPs, especially during update events. Validate the digital signatures and hashes of update packages and all binaries written to disk. Alert if the updater writes or executes files not present in official manifests or if unsigned executables are launched. Correlate process creation events with update activity to detect unauthorized payload execution.
